title: Jak X: Combat Racing
subtitle: A race with an antidote at the finish
summary: Jak X: Combat Racing is Naughty Dog's PlayStation 2 vehicular combat game, first released in North America on 18 October 2005. body: Jak X: Combat Racing is Naughty Dog's PlayStation 2 vehicular combat game, first released in North America on 18 October 2005. Jak and his companions are poisoned and forced to enter a dangerous racing championship to obtain an antidote. The spin-off turns the driving introduced in Jak 3 into the centre of a complete game. Customisable buggies compete through circuits where destroying an opponent can be as useful as passing them. The story gives the familiar cast a reason to remain in the driver's seat rather than return to a platform adventure.

Pickups connect the series' Eco to practical racing tools. Yellow supplies offensive weapons, red provides defensive options, green restores health and blue adds turbo. The player must keep a racing line while deciding how these resources can change the surrounding contest. Damage also builds a Dark Eco meter that strengthens weapons when filled. Championship events award progress through the adventure, while individual races give a reason to learn a course more closely. A clean lap remains valuable, but the next opponent can interrupt it with more than a better corner.

Jak X became the first game in the series to include multiplayer, allowing the combat-racing rules to work between human drivers as well as through the campaign. Amy Hennig directed the project, with music by Billy Howerdel, Dean Menta and Larry Hopkins giving it a harder sound. Save data from related games could unlock additional drivers, connecting the roster to other PlayStation releases. A later PlayStation 4 edition kept the game available beside the original trilogy. It remains a substantial variation on the series, built around racing systems that had previously supported only part of its adventures.
